conflicts.topic: what identity proof a non-EU newcomer needs to get banking codes enabled for strong identification
conflicts.aQuote: Banks in Finland require a foreigner’s identity card issued by the Finnish authorities to enable non-EU nationals use online banking credentials for strong identification
conflicts.bQuote: Nordea describes a workaround used in Finland: you can visit a police station, where your identity is verified so the electronic identification service can be activated
conflicts.note: International House Helsinki says banks require a Finnish-issued foreigner's ID card for non-EU nationals; Nordic Expat says Nordea has a police-station identity check as a workaround when you lack an accepted document.
conflicts.whatToDo: Treat the International House Helsinki checklist as the baseline, and bring your Finnish-issued residence or ID card and your personal identity code to the bank visit. If you have no document the bank accepts, ask the bank directly whether it offers a route such as a police identity check, because this comes from a community site and banks decide their own procedures. Ask explicitly for codes enabled for strong electronic identification, not only for online banking.
